items.stem: During a case the monitor shows ventricular fibrillation and the patient is unresponsive. What is the first priority action?

options.text: Document the event in detail first
options.rationale: Documentation must not delay life-saving intervention.

options.text: Initiate defibrillation and resuscitation per protocol
options.rationale: Correct: pulseless VF requires immediate defibrillation and CPR per ACLS.

options.text: Wait for a second rhythm confirmation over several minutes
options.rationale: Delaying defibrillation in pulseless VF worsens outcomes.
Removing monitoring hinders care during an arrest.

items.explanation: Correct: pulseless VF requires immediate defibrillation and CPR per ACLS.

items.stem: A pressure waveform shows a rapid upstroke and a dicrotic notch. Which structure is most likely being measured?

options.rationale: Venous pressures are low and lack an arterial dicrotic notch.
Correct: a sharp upstroke with a dicrotic notch is characteristic of an arterial/aortic waveform.
The lymphatic system is not pressure-monitored this way.
The esophagus is not a cardiovascular pressure site.

items.explanation: Correct: a sharp upstroke with a dicrotic notch is characteristic of an arterial/aortic waveform.

items.stem: Which TWO actions maintain sterile integrity in the cath lab?

options.text: Keeping sterile items above waist level and within the sterile field
options.rationale: Correct: items below waist level or out of view are considered contaminated.

options.text: Performing surgical hand antisepsis and donning sterile attire
options.rationale: Correct: proper hand antisepsis and sterile gowning/gloving preserve sterility.

options.text: Reaching across the sterile field with ungloved hands
options.rationale: Reaching across with ungloved hands contaminates the field.
Reusing single-use items breaches sterility and safety.

items.explanation: Correct: items below waist level or out of view are considered contaminated.
